source_text:
Μετὰ ἡμέρας ὀλίγας εἶδον αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ πεδίον τὸ αὐτό, ὅπου καὶ τοὺς ποιμένας ἑωράκειν, καὶ λέγει μοι: Τί ἐπιζητεῖς; Πάρειμι, κύριε, ἵνα τὸν ποιμένα τὸν τιμωρητὴν κελεύσῃς ἐκ τοῦ οἴκου μου ἐξελθεῖν, ὅτι λίαν με θλίβει. Δεῖ σε, φησί, θλιβῆναι: οὕτω γάρ, φησί, προσέταξεν ὁ ἔνδοξος ἄγγελος τὰ περὶ σοῦ: θέλει γάρ σε πειρασθῆναι. Τί γάρ, φημί, κύριε, ἐποίησα οὕτω πονηρόν, ἵνα τῷ ἀγγέλῳ τούτῳ παραδοθῶ;
Ἄκουε, φησίν: αἱ μὲν ἁμαρτίαι σου πολλαί, ἀλλ’ οὐ τοσαῦται, ὥστε τῷ ἀγγέλῳ τούτῳ παραδοθῆναι: ἀλλ’ ὁ οἶκός σου μεγάλας ἀνομίας καὶ ἁμαρτίας εἰργάσατο, καὶ παρεπικράνθη ὁ ἔνδοξος ἄγγελος ἐπὶ τοῖς ἔργοις αὐτῶν καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ἐκέλευσέ σε χρόνον τινὰ θλιβῆναι, ἵνα κἀκεῖνοι μετανοήσωσι καὶ καθαρίσωσιν ἑαυτοὺς ἀπὸ πάσης ἐπιθυμίας τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου. ὅταν οὖν μετανοήσωσι καὶ καθαρισθῶσι, τότε ἀποστήσεται ἀπὸ σοῦ ὁ ἄγγελος τῆς τιμωρίας.
λέγω αὐτῷ: Κύριε, εἰ ἐκεῖνοι τοιαῦτα εἰργάσαντο, ἵνα παραπικρανθῇ ὁ ἔνδοξος ἄγγελος, τί ἐγὼ ἐποίησα; Ἄλλως, φησίν, οὐ δύνανται ἐκεῖνοι θλιβῆναι, ἐὰν μὴ σὺ ἡ κεφαλὴ τοῦ οἴκου θλιβῇς: σοῦ γὰρ θλιβομένου ἐξ ἀνάγκης κἀκεῖνοι θλιβήσονται, εὐσταθοῦντος δὲ σοῦ οὐδεμίαν δύνανται θλῖψιν ἔχειν.
Ἀλλ’ ἰδού, φημί, κύριε, μετανενοήκασιν ἐξ ὅλης καρδίας αὐτῶν. Οἶδα, φησί, κἀγώ, ὅτι μετανενοήκασιν ἐξ ὅλης καρδίας αὐτῶν: τῶν οὖν μετανοούντων εὐθὺς δοκεῖς τὰς ἁμαρτιας ἀφίεσθαι; οὐ παντελῶς: ἀλλὰ δεῖ τὸν μετανοοῦντα βασανίσαι τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ψυχὴν καὶ ταπεινοφρονῆσαι ἐν πάσῃ πράξει αὐτοῦ ἰσχυρῶς καὶ θλιβῆναι ἐν πάσαις θίψεσι ποικίλαις: καὶ ἐὰν ὑπενέγκῃ τὰς θλίψεις τὰς ἐπερχομένας αὐτῷ, πάντως σπλαγχνισθήσεται ὁ τὰ πάντα κτίσας καὶ ἐνδυναμώσας καὶ ἴασίν τινα δώσει αὐτῷ:
καὶ τοῦτο πάντως, ἐὰν ἴδῃ τὴν καρδίαν τοῦ μετανοοῦντος καθαρὰν ἀπὸ παντὸς πονηροῦ πράγματος. σοὶ δὲ συμφέρον ἐστὶ καὶ τῷ οἴκῳ σου νῦν θλιβῆναι. τί δέ σοι πολλὰ λέγω; θλιβῆναί σε δεῖ, καθὼς προσέταξεν ὁ ἄγγελος κυρίου ἐκεῖνος, ὁ παραδιδούς σε ἐμοί: καὶ τοῦτο εὐχαρίστει τῷ κυρίῳ, ὅτι ἄξιόν σε ἡγήσατο τοῦ προδηλῶσαί σοι τὴν θλῖψιν, ἵνα προγνοὺς αὐτὴν ὑπενέγκῃς ἰσχυρῶς.
λέγω αὐτῷ: Κύριε, σὺ μετ’ ἐμοῦ γίνου, καὶ δυνήσομαι πᾶσαν θλῖψιν ὑπενεγκεῖν. Ἐγώ, φησίν, ἔσομαι μετὰ σοῦ: ἐρωτήσω δέ καὶ τὸν ἄγγελον τὸν τιμωρητήν, ἵνα σε ἐλαφροτέρως θλίψῃ: ἀλλ’ ὀλίγον χρόνον θλιβήσῃ καὶ πάλιν ἀποκατασταθήσῃ εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου. μόνον παράμεινον ταπεινοφρονῶν καὶ λειτουργῶν τῷ κυρίῳ ἐν πάσῃ καθαρᾷ καρδίᾳ, καὶ τὰ τέκνα σου καὶ ὁ οἶκός σου, καὶ πορεύου ἐν ταῖς ἐντολαῖς μου αἷς σοι ἐντέλλομαι, καὶ δυνήσεταί σου ἡ μετάνοια ἰσχυρὰ καὶ καθαρὰ εἶναι:
καὶ ἐὰν ταύτας φυλάξῃς μετὰ τοῦ οἴκου σου, ἀποστήσεται πᾶσα θλῖψις ἀπὸ σοῦ: καὶ ἀπὸ πάντων δέ, φησίν, ἀποστήσεται θλῖψις. ὅσοι ἐὰν ἐν ταῖς ἐντολαῖς μου ταύταις πορευθῶσιν.
thought_title: The head of the house must be afflicted so the household may repent
orientation: A few days later Hermas meets the Shepherd in the same plain and asks him to send away the angel of punishment, who is now in his own house. The Shepherd explains why Hermas must suffer for a time.
pass_a_gloss: After a few days I saw him in the same plain, where also I had seen the shepherds, and he says to me: What do you seek? I am here, lord, so that you may command the punishing shepherd to go out from my house, because he afflicts me greatly. You must, he says, be afflicted: for thus, he says, the glorious angel commanded the things concerning you: for he wishes you to be tested. For what, I say, lord, did I do so evil, that I should be handed over to this angel? Listen, he says: your sins are many, but not so many, that you should be handed over to this angel: but your house committed great lawless deeds and sins, and the glorious angel was provoked to anger at their works and because of this he commanded you to be afflicted for some time, so that they also may repent and cleanse themselves from every desire of this age. When therefore they repent and are cleansed, then the angel of punishment will depart from you. I say to him: Lord, if they did such things, that the glorious angel was provoked to anger, what did I do? Otherwise, he says, they cannot be afflicted, unless you the head of the house are afflicted: for when you are afflicted, of necessity they also will be afflicted, but when you are prospering, they cannot have any tribulation. But behold, I say, lord, they have repented from their whole heart. I know, he says, I also, that they have repented from their whole heart: do you think then that the sins of those who repent are forgiven immediately? Not at all: but the one who repents must torment his own soul and humble himself in every deed of his strongly and be afflicted in various tribulations of every kind: and if he endures the tribulations that come upon him, certainly the one who created all things and strengthened and will give some healing to him will be moved with compassion: and this certainly, if he sees the heart of the one who repents clean from every evil thing. But for you and your house it is beneficial now to be afflicted. But why do I say many things to you? You must be afflicted, just as that angel of the Lord commanded, the one who handed you over to me: and for this give thanks to the Lord, because he considered you worthy to reveal to you beforehand the tribulation, so that knowing it beforehand you may endure it strongly. I say to him: Lord, be with me, and I will be able to endure every tribulation. I, he says, will be with you: and I will ask also the punishing angel, that he may afflict you more lightly: but for a little time you will be afflicted and again you will be restored to your house. Only remain humbling yourself and serving the Lord in all clean heart, and your children and your house, and walk in my commandments which I command you, and your repentance will be able to be strong and clean: and if you keep these with your house, every tribulation will depart from you: and from all, he says, tribulation will depart, as many as walk in these my commandments.

choices.why: Literal rendering of the noun with its adjectival modifier; the glossary identifies this figure as the angel of punishment, but the source here uses ποιμήν, so the literal lane keeps 'shepherd'.
The compound verb παραπικραίνω means to embitter or provoke to anger; the passive form here indicates the glorious angel's reaction to the household's deeds.
The genitive absolute with εὐσταθέω means being in good condition or prospering; the contrast with θλιβομένου (being afflicted) is preserved.
The verb βασανίζω means to torment or torture; the reflexive pronoun ἑαυτοῦ emphasizes the self-inflicted nature of the affliction required of the repentant.
The verb σπλαγχνίζομαι refers to being moved in the inward parts, the seat of compassion; the passive form is rendered with the full phrase to capture the emotional force.

choices.english: to reveal to you beforehand the tribulation
choices.why: The compound verb προδηλόω means to make clear beforehand; the prefix προ- is essential to the argument that Hermas is given advance knowledge so he can endure.
rejected: to make known to you the tribulation

pass_b_english: A few days later I saw the Shepherd in the same plain where I had seen the shepherds, and he said to me, “What are you seeking?”
“Sir,” I said, “I am here so that you may order the punishing shepherd to leave my house, for he afflicts me greatly.”
“You must be afflicted,” he said. “For this is what the glorious angel has commanded concerning you. He wants you to be tested.”
“But what have I done, sir,” I said, “that is so evil that I should be handed over to this angel?”

“Listen,” he said. “Your sins are many, but not so many that you should be handed over to this angel. But your household has committed great acts of lawlessness and sin, and the glorious angel was bitterly provoked by what they did. That is why he ordered you to be afflicted for a time, so that they too may repent and cleanse themselves of every desire of this age. So when they repent and are cleansed, then the angel of punishment will depart from you.”
I said to him, “Sir, if they have done such things that the glorious angel is bitterly provoked, what have I done?”

“There is no other way for them to be afflicted,” he said, “unless you, the head of the house, are afflicted. For when you are afflicted, they too are bound to be afflicted. But while you are at ease, they can have no tribulation.”
“But look, sir,” I said, “they have repented with their whole heart.”

“I know it too,” he said. “They have repented with their whole heart. But do you think that the sins of those who repent are forgiven at once? Not at all. The one who repents must torment his own soul. He must be deeply humble in all he does, and be afflicted with tribulations of every kind. And if he bears the tribulations that come upon him, the one who created all things and gave them strength will surely be moved with compassion and will give him some healing.

“And he will surely do this, if he sees that the heart of the one who repents is pure of every evil thing. But it is to your benefit, and your household’s, to be afflicted now. Why should I say more to you? You must be afflicted, as that angel of the Lord commanded, the one who handed you over to me. And give thanks to the Lord for this: he counted you worthy to be shown the tribulation beforehand, so that, knowing of it in advance, you may bear it with strength.”
I said to him, “Sir, be with me, and I will be able to bear every tribulation.”

“I will be with you,” he said. “I will also ask the punishing angel to afflict you more lightly. Still, you will be afflicted for a little while, and then you will be restored to your house. Only continue to be humble and to minister to the Lord with a wholly pure heart, you and your children and your household. Walk in my commandments, which I am giving you, and your repentance can be strong and pure.
“And if you keep these commandments together with your household, every tribulation will depart from you. Yes,” he said, “and tribulation will depart from all who walk in these commandments of mine.”

problems.why: 'Prospering' implies wealth/success; εὐσταθοῦντος means 'standing firm, being stable, at ease'.
problems.ruling: εὐσταθοῦντος means 'standing firm/stable'; 'prospering' misleadingly implies material success, changing the contrast with θλιβοῦ.

edits.old: but when you are prospering, they cannot experience any tribulation.
edits.new: but when you are at ease, they cannot experience any tribulation.

polish.changed: Clarified speaker transitions, resolved ambiguous pronouns, smoothed sentence flow for oral reading, and removed em dashes while preserving every claim and qualification.

notes.why: Noun, adjective, and verb forms used for same concept; reader may miss connection

notes.quote: the shepherd, the angel of repentance
notes.why: The same figure is called 'the shepherd,' 'the angel of repentance,' and 'the Shepherd' with inconsistent capitalization.
notes.fix: Standardize to 'the Shepherd (the angel of repentance)'.

notes.why: The same angel who hands Hermas over to the Shepherd is called by different titles.
notes.fix: Use one title consistently, e.g., 'the glorious angel'.

last_rejected.ruling: Source says τὸν ποιμένα τὸν τιμωρητὴν; 'punishing shepherd' is literal and accurate. No glossary evidence shown.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'angel of punishment', not 'punishing angel'.
last_rejected.ruling: τὸν ἄγγελον τὸν τιμωρητήν = 'the punishing angel'; both adjective and noun match. No glossary conflict demonstrated.

last_rejected.why: θλίβει here means 'oppresses/troubles', not 'afflicts' in the theological sense; but worse, 'afflicting' anticipates the later technical term θλῖψις/tribulation.
last_rejected.fix: because he is oppressing me greatly
last_rejected.ruling: θλίβω covers 'afflict/oppress'; same root as θλῖψις, so consistency is reasonable, not a meaning change.
